outcome: composite of immediate postpartum complications (vaso-occlusive pain events, acute chest syndrome, infection, new-onset hypoxia)
cohort: The study assessed 201 pregnancies from 145 individuals with sickle cell disease (SCD) between 2000 and 2018.
finding: Hypoxia during pregnancy and unscheduled caesarean delivery were identified as the strongest risk factors for immediate postpartum complications in pregnant individuals with SCD.
mod_finding: Unscheduled caesarean delivery was a strong risk factor associated with immediate postpartum complications.
followup_time: from admission during delivery to discharge (immediate postpartum period)
